tariffRates.additionalInfo: Trade war tensions may affect future rates. Consider alternative suppliers from India or Germany for better duty rates.
EU-India trade agreement negotiations may reduce tariffs significantly by Q2 2025.

Electrical connectors from Japan currently qualify for a 1% import duty under the EU-Japan trade agreement. To qualify for the lower rate, the product must be made or significantly processed in Japan. Your Japanese supplier must provide a short "statement of origin" on the invoice that proves this. 
The preferential rate will fall to 0% on 2025-02-01 as part of the EU-Japan free trade agreement. No quotas or trade restrictions apply to these parts.

Imports of aluminium profiles from China face a 7.5% tariff plus a 25% anti-dumping duty, totaling 32.5%. The EU has renewed these measures several times, so they are a long-term structural cost when sourcing from China. The next review of these measures is December 2025, after which the rates may increase or decrease.
For now, costs will remain high. Consider shifting part of your sourcing to Turkey or EU suppliers, which benefit from zero tariffs under the EU-Turkey Customs Union.

U.S. import duty on German sensor sub-assemblies rose from 2.5% MFN rate to 27.5% effective 2025-05-03 as part of new US tariffs on automobiles and auto parts. In September 2025 this rate was reduced to 15% (effective 2025-08-01) as part of trade negotiations between the EU and US. There is no free-trade agreement to offset this rate, which is expected to remain through 2026. U.S. buyers now face higher landed costs, so you may need to adjust pricing or consider partial production in a lower-tariff region.

Past Week.title: Aluminium profiles (HS 7604.21 – China)
Past Week.description: EU Official Journal confirmed that the anti-dumping duty review will close on Dec 1 2025 with rates expected to remain unchanged (≈ 25 %). No immediate cost change, but signals continuity through 2026.

Past Week.title: Electrical connectors (HS 8536.69 – Japan)
Past Week.description: EU–Japan EPA Secretariat issued an advisory notice clarifying supplier statement wording ahead of the final 0 % duty step-down on 1 Feb 2025. Importers should check invoices already use the new text.

Past Week.title: Steel bolts/screws (HS 7318.15 – Taiwan)
Past Week.description: DG Trade opened a public consultation on proposed safeguard quotas. Not binding yet, but if adopted could lift duties from 3.7 → 5 %.

Past Month.title: Copper wire (HS 7408.19 – Kazakhstan)
Past Month.description: Anti-circumvention inquiry launched by the Commission to test whether KZ exports contain Russian content. Could add +2 % duty from Mar 2026 if confirmed.

Past Month.title: Wiring harness cable (HS 8544.30 – Morocco)
Past Month.description: EU–Morocco trade committee published revised origin thresholds (value-added rising to 60 %). Takes effect Jan 2026; qualifying suppliers unaffected.

Past Month.title: Cold-rolled steel sheet (HS 7209.16 – India)
Past Month.description: Safeguard proposal filed to double MFN rate from 2 → 4 % by Nov 2025. Still at "proposed" stage.

Past 3 Months.title: EU–Japan EPA (HS 8536.69 etc.)
Past 3 Months.description: Mid-term EPA review formally opened. Confirms that all electrical parts under 8536 will become duty-free on 1 Feb 2025.

Past 3 Months.title: EU–Morocco & Tunisia FTAs
Past 3 Months.description: Both agreements updated administrative rules for origin documentation; no duty change, but new supplier-statement templates effective Q1 2026.

Past 3 Months.title: Aluminium & steel measures
Past 3 Months.description: EU extended surveillance on semi-finished metals imports from China, India, Vietnam — tighter reporting but not new duties yet.

Past 3 Months.title: CBAM phase-in
Past 3 Months.description: EU published the 2026 CBAM reporting list, confirming aluminium products (HS 76) will be covered from Jan 2026 — adds emissions-reporting obligation, not a tariff.

Past Year.title: Anti-dumping renewals
Past Year.description: Aluminium profiles from China remained under 25 % AD duty, extended for another five years (through 2030).

Past Year.title: Tariff reductions under FTAs
Past Year.description: Multiple staged cuts under EU–Japan, EU–Vietnam, and EU–UK agreements reached their 2025 rate milestones (e.g., 8536 from 1 % → 0 %).

Past Year.title: CBAM implementation (pilot phase)
Past Year.description: Importers of iron, steel, aluminium began quarterly carbon reporting in Oct 2024; no monetary charge yet but groundwork for 2026 levy.

Past Year.title: Trade defense climate
Past Year.description: EU initiated or renewed 11 anti-dumping cases on metals, fasteners, and cables since late 2024 — confirming a tougher stance that's unlikely to reverse soon.

Past Week.title: UK (EU–UK TCA)
Past Week.description: The UK government published a new template for supplier origin declarations, valid from January 2026. This replaces the 2021 version but keeps the same 0% duty treatment for qualifying EU goods.

Past Week.title: U.S.
Past Week.description: USTR confirmed review hearings for the new 15% tariffs on EU industrial goods will begin February 2026, establishing the next policy milestone.

Past Month.title: UK
Past Month.description: HMRC issued guidance reminding importers that statements of origin older than 12 months will no longer be accepted from January 2026.

Past Month.title: U.S.
Past Month.description: The U.S.–EU Reciprocal Tariff Framework officially entered into the Federal Register, confirming the 15% rate effective 1 Aug 2025 for auto-related goods (including HS 8538 / 8544).

Past Month.title: Switzerland
Past Month.description: Swiss customs announced a 2026 rollout of e-origin certification, allowing digital proof of origin under the EU–CH FTA.

Past 3 Months.title: UK
Past 3 Months.description: The EU and UK trade committees formally reviewed TCA implementation for automotive parts. While no rule changes were made, both sides endorsed digitalisation of RoO records for 2026.

Past 3 Months.title: U.S.
Past 3 Months.description: Implementation of the 15% tariff (effective August 1) replaced the prior 2.6% MFN rate for EU-made industrial components.

Past 3 Months.title: Norway
Past 3 Months.description: The EFTA Secretariat published draft rules for electronic EUR.1 certificates, to be adopted across EEA members in early 2026.

Past 3 Months.title: Switzerland
Past 3 Months.description: Bilateral working group approved updates to FTA administrative annexes, paving the way for e-certificates and simplified audits.

Past Year.title: U.S.
Past Year.description: The U.S. imposed 15% tariffs on EU autos and industrial parts (incl. 8538 / 8544) under the new reciprocal trade framework. This is the most significant change affecting HanseAuto's U.S. sales.

Past Year.title: UK
Past Year.description: The EU–UK TCA "transition phase" for simplified origin proofs ended in mid-2025. Starting 2026, the UK requires stricter origin statements with specific validity windows.

Past Year.title: Norway / Switzerland
Past Year.description: Both FTA partners confirmed participation in the EU's 2026 digital certificate initiative, harmonising e-origin processes across the region.

upcomingChangesData.title: Aluminium profiles (HS 7604.21 – China)
upcomingChangesData.description: The EU's anti-dumping review closes in December 2025. The current 25% surcharge is widely expected to continue, possibly with minor adjustments.
upcomingChangesData.impact: No cost relief; keep exploring EU or Turkish sources.
upcomingChangesData.timing: December 2025 decision; new rates (if any) from January 2026.

upcomingChangesData.title: Cold-rolled steel sheet (HS 7209.16 – India)
upcomingChangesData.description: A safeguard proposal could double the duty from 2% → 4%.
upcomingChangesData.impact: Cost increase of roughly €20 per ton if approved.
upcomingChangesData.timing: Proposal under DG Trade review; outcome expected November 2025.

upcomingChangesData.title: Copper wire (HS 7408.19 – Kazakhstan)
upcomingChangesData.description: The EU's anti-circumvention probe continues; potential +2% duty if Russian-origin material confirmed.

upcomingChangesData.title: Electrical connectors (HS 8536.69 – Japan)
upcomingChangesData.description: Final EU–Japan tariff cut to 0% takes effect 1 February 2025, completing the EPA phase-in.
upcomingChangesData.impact: Small but permanent savings; confirm supplier origin documentation before year-end.

upcomingChangesData.title: Wiring harness cable (HS 8544.30 – Morocco/Tunisia)
upcomingChangesData.description: Revised rules of origin come into force in early 2026, requiring slightly higher local content for 0% duty.
upcomingChangesData.impact: No duty change if suppliers are compliant, but paperwork must follow the new template.

upcomingChangesData.title: Plastic fasteners (HS 3926.30 – China)
upcomingChangesData.description: EU Trade Defence Service has flagged this category for a potential safeguard screening in mid-2026.
upcomingChangesData.impact: Low probability of action, but under monitoring.

upcomingChangesData.title: CBAM (Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism)
upcomingChangesData.description: From January 2026, importers of aluminium and steel products must start emissions reporting under CBAM.
upcomingChangesData.impact: Administrative only in 2026, but financial charges start in 2027; early data collection recommended.

upcomingChangesData.title: Origin documentation refresh
upcomingChangesData.description: Several FTAs (Japan, Morocco, UK) have new supplier statement formats effective in early 2026.
upcomingChangesData.impact: Low; ensure procurement teams receive updated templates.

exportUpcomingChangesData.title: United Kingdom (EU–UK TCA)
exportUpcomingChangesData.description: The UK and EU are tightening the rules-of-origin process for all goods traded duty-free under the Trade and Cooperation Agreement. New declaration formats and expiry periods for supplier statements take effect January 2026. Automotive and electronics parts like wiring harnesses and sensor assemblies remain 0% duty if origin proofs are valid.
exportUpcomingChangesData.impact: No tariff change, but missing or outdated paperwork would trigger UK MFN rates (2–3%).
exportUpcomingChangesData.action: Refresh origin documentation with suppliers by December 2025 to keep duty-free status.

exportUpcomingChangesData.title: United States
exportUpcomingChangesData.description: The 15% U.S. import tariff on EU industrial goods is expected to remain in place through at least 2027, but Washington and Brussels are due to review the framework in mid-2026. USTR has also hinted that some components may be recategorized under a new 'essential industrial goods' list, which might lower rates on specific subheadings such as electrical parts (HS 8538, 8544).
exportUpcomingChangesData.impact: No change to current pricing in 2025, but a policy window in 2026 could open for partial rollback or product-specific exclusions.
exportUpcomingChangesData.action: Track the 2026 review timetable and maintain dialogue with U.S. distributors about requesting exclusion status for low-risk automotive parts.

exportUpcomingChangesData.title: Norway (EEA Agreement)
exportUpcomingChangesData.description: The EEA digital certificate rollout will replace the paper EUR.1 origin form in Q1 2026. No duty change; Norway continues to apply 0% tariff on EU-origin goods.
exportUpcomingChangesData.impact: Only administrative—ensure export paperwork migrates to the new format.
exportUpcomingChangesData.action: Update ERP templates and train the shipping team before March 2026.

exportUpcomingChangesData.title: Switzerland (EU–CH FTA)
exportUpcomingChangesData.description: The EU–Switzerland trade modernization program introduces new supplier statement templates and e-certification options in early 2026. Duty stays 0% with origin proof.
exportUpcomingChangesData.impact: Minimal, but incorrect documents could delay clearance.
exportUpcomingChangesData.action: Adopt the new statement wording in Q1 2026.
